stem: Which blood film feature most supports a reactive lymphocyte rather than a leukaemic blast?

options.text: More abundant cytoplasm with broader morphologic diversity
A nucleolus is the key reassuring feature
Concurrent thrombocytopaenia confirms a reactive process
Reactive lymphocytes and blasts are morphologically indistinguishable

explanation: More abundant cytoplasm with broader morphologic diversity is the feature that best supports a reactive lymphocyte rather than a leukaemic blast.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because reactive lymphocytes typically have more abundant cytoplasm and greater variation in morphology than leukaemic blasts.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a uniform cell with no cytoplasm is more in keeping with a blast than a reactive lymphocyte.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reactive lymphocytes are not identified by a nucleolus as the reassuring feature; they are more often recognised by their abundant cytoplasm and variable appearance.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because thrombocytopaenia does not confirm a reactive process and may raise concern for leukaemia or other marrow pathology.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because although reactive lymphocytes can resemble blasts, they are not morphologically indistinguishable.
